Read and Filter an MZmine Full Feature Table

read_mzmine_feature_table.Rd

Usage

read_mzmine_feature_table(
  file,
  min_detect_fraction = 0.5,
  area_col = c("area", "height"),
  clean_names = TRUE,
  keep_meta = TRUE,
  zero_as_na = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

file

character(1). Path to the MZmine full feature table CSV (e.g. "test_1_full_feature_table.csv").

min_detect_fraction

numeric(1). Minimum fraction of samples (0–1) in which a feature must have a non-zero area to be retained. Defaults to 0.5 (50 \

area_colcharacter(1). Which per-sample intensity metric to extract. One of "area" (default) or "height".

clean_nameslogical(1). If TRUE (default), strip the "datafile:" prefix and ".mzXML:area" (or ":height") suffix from column names, leaving only the bare sample names.

keep_metalogical(1). If TRUE (default), prepend the consensus columns id, mz, and rt to the output. Set to FALSE to return a pure sample-by-feature matrix.

zero_as_nalogical(1). If TRUE, replace all zero area values with NA before returning. Useful for log-transformation workflows. Defaults to FALSE.

verboselogical(1). If TRUE (default), print a short summary of features before and after filtering, plus the number of samples detected.

A tibble with one row per retained feature. If keep_meta = TRUE the first three columns are id, mz, and rt, followed by one column per sample. If keep_meta = FALSE only the sample columns are returned (with row names set to the feature id values, if the result is coerced to a data.frame). Imports an MZmine 3 *_feature_table.csv file, extracts per-sample peak-area columns, optionally renames them to bare sample names, and filters out features that were not detected in a minimum fraction of samples. MZmine 3 names every per-sample column with the pattern datafile:<sample_filename>.<ext>:<metric>. This function uses a regex on the column suffix (:area or :height) to identify sample columns, so it is robust to mixed file extensions (.mzML, .mzXML, .raw, etc.).Features with feature_state == "ESTIMATED" (gap-filled) are treated identically to "DETECTED" features for filtering purposes; only cells containing NA or 0 count as "not detected".
